key_insight: A Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic interface can respond to shock-driven Richtmyer-Meshkov perturbations in either oscillatory or monotonic early-time modes, with a critical viscoelastic number separating the two behaviors.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretical criterion for predicting how shock-loaded soft materials, fluids, and viscoelastic solids will evolve immediately after impact, which is useful for blast and injury mechanics.
method: Linear stability analysis of the incompressible Cauchy momentum equation
Kelvin-Voigt constitutive model for two viscoelastic materials
Implicit dispersion relation derived for single-mode perturbation growth rates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparison across four material cases spanning symmetric to highly contrasted interfaces to show how viscoelastic number, density contrast, and viscosity contrast change the growth-rate structure.
watch_item: The result is a linear, early-time theory for single-mode perturbations, so nonlinear effects and later-time interface evolution are not captured.
paper_title: Early-time dynamics of the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic interfaces
